name: Dusty Lavender
lede: Dusty Lavender is a pale, greyed purple close to the real flower [[lavender]], listed in the ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary as well as the 2010 xkcd survey.

sections.title: Closer to the real flower
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary places this color in its block 214, among colors it calls "pale violet", 4.0 units away in our conversion, one of the closer matches in our library [1]. The 2010 xkcd crowd survey records the same word separately [2]. In Munsell terms it reads about 8.5P 6.0/5.8, a light, moderately desaturated purple [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[heather]], [[opera-mauve]] and [[phlox-pink]], at 2.9, 3.1 and 4.2 ΔE [1]. Its nearest cousins in our data are [[mauve]], a touch pinker, and [[dusty-purple]], darker and greyer still [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, one of the rarer matches among our color names, as photographed [3]. All three are Post-Impressionist or early-modern works, including Henri-Edmond Cross's 1896 *[[painting:cma-84371|The Pink Cloud]]* and Paul Sérusier's 1894 *[[painting:commons-Q17493118|Le Pardon de Notre-Dame-des-Portes à Châteauneuf-du-Faou]]* [3]. In every match it plays a mid-tone, never a shadow or a highlight [3]. Too few paintings share it to name a leading country or decade with confidence beyond noting that all three sit in France [3]. These counts are a computed color match on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not a pigment test [3].
